title: Sessions and tokens survive process restart
description: The session store and the sign-in token store are backed by durable storage that survives a process restart. A process restart of the authenticating service does not invalidate outstanding sessions, does not reset idle-expiry clocks, and does not consume-then-lose in-flight sign-in tokens. The blueprint does not fix the storage engine; the project supplies the durable store through the session-manager and magic-link-manager interfaces.
rationale: In-memory sessions turn every deploy into a forced logout for every operator, which teaches the operator to distrust the sign-out button when it does happen. Persistent storage is the difference between authentication that outlives the process and authentication that pretends to.
